11.title: Parse a Lesson Count: catch NumberFormatException
11.description: Implement `parseLessonCount(String text)` to return Integer.parseInt(text), or -1 when parsing throws NumberFormatException.
11.learningObjective: Handle invalid integer text with a specific unchecked exception and preserve the valid result.
instructions: Call Integer.parseInt inside try.
Catch NumberFormatException only.
Return the parsed integer after successful conversion.
Return -1 after invalid numeric text.

workedExample.explanation: Catching the expected conversion exception keeps invalid user input recoverable without hiding unrelated programming defects.

11.hint: Integer.parseInt throws NumberFormatException when text is not a valid integer.
11.explanation: Catching the expected conversion exception keeps invalid user input recoverable without hiding unrelated programming defects.

testCases.description: Parse with Integer.parseInt.
Catch NumberFormatException.
Return the parsed value on success.
Return -1 on invalid text.

12.title: Close a Reader Safely: use try-with-resources
12.description: Read one line from a StringReader inside try-with-resources and return it. The resource must be declared in the try header so Java closes it automatically.
12.learningObjective: Use try-with-resources to close an AutoCloseable resource even when reading fails.
instructions: Import BufferedReader and StringReader.
Create the StringReader and BufferedReader in the try resource header.
Read and return the first line from the try body.
Do not call close manually after the try block.

workedExample.explanation: Try-with-resources reduces leaks and still closes the resource if the body throws. Both reader types implement AutoCloseable through Closeable.

12.hint: A resource declared in a try-with-resources header is closed automatically at the end of that statement.
12.explanation: Try-with-resources reduces leaks and still closes the resource if the body throws. Both reader types implement AutoCloseable through Closeable.

testCases.description: Declare the reader resources in the try header.
Read one line.
Return the line.
Rely on automatic closing.

12.expectedOutput:
REFERENCE EXAMPLE · NOT A PROGRAM RUN

Close a Reader Safely: use try-with-resources

Input: readFirstLine("HTML lessons")

Expected value: "HTML lessons"

Try-with-resources reduces leaks and still closes the resource if the body throws. Both reader types implement AutoCloseable through Closeable.

13.title: Handle Two Parse Failures: use multi-catch
13.description: Implement `parseIndex(String text)` to parse `text.trim()` and return -1 for either NumberFormatException or NullPointerException. Trimming exposes null input as a null reference failure, while malformed text causes a parse failure. Use one multi-catch clause with both exception types.
13.learningObjective: Use a multi-catch clause for two related input failures that share the same recovery behavior.
instructions: Call text.trim() and parse the result inside try.
Use one catch clause with NumberFormatException and NullPointerException separated by a vertical bar.
Return -1 from the shared recovery block.
Return the parsed index on success.

workedExample.explanation: A shared recovery action can use multi-catch to avoid duplicating a catch body. The alternative exception types cannot be subclasses of one another.

13.hint: Multi-catch uses the | separator when multiple unrelated exception types share one response.
13.explanation: A shared recovery action can use multi-catch to avoid duplicating a catch body. The alternative exception types cannot be subclasses of one another.

testCases.description: Trim text before parsing so null produces NullPointerException.
Catch both named exception types in one multi-catch.
Return -1 after either input failure.
Return the parsed integer on success.

13.expectedOutput:

Handle Two Parse Failures: use multi-catch

Input: parseIndex(null)

Expected value: -1

A shared recovery action can use multi-catch to avoid duplicating a catch body. The alternative exception types cannot be subclasses of one another.

14.title: Declare the Checked Failure: use throws
14.description: Implement `readFirst(BufferedReader reader)` to return reader.readLine(). Declare IOException with throws instead of catching it inside the helper.
14.learningObjective: Declare a checked IOException in a method signature and let its caller decide how to handle it.
instructions: Return reader.readLine() from the helper.
Add throws IOException to the method declaration.
Do not add a catch block in this helper.
Keep the caller responsible for handling or declaring the checked exception.

workedExample.output: The first line, or null at end of input
workedExample.explanation: Declaring a checked exception makes the failure visible to callers, allowing a higher layer to choose an appropriate response.

14.hint: A checked exception can be propagated by listing its type after throws in the method signature.
14.explanation: Declaring a checked exception makes the failure visible to callers, allowing a higher layer to choose an appropriate response.

15.title: Invalid Course Level: create a domain exception
15.description: Define `InvalidCourseLevelException` as a subclass of Exception. Implement `validateLevel(int level)` to accept 1 through 100 inclusive and throw the custom exception otherwise.
15.learningObjective: Create a checked domain exception for a course level outside the supported range.
instructions: Declare the custom exception class extending Exception.
Give it a constructor that forwards a message to super.
Declare validateLevel with throws InvalidCourseLevelException.
Throw for values below 1 or above 100; accept both boundaries.

workedExample.explanation: A domain exception can name a business-rule failure more precisely than a generic exception. The method contract makes the checked failure explicit to callers.

15.hint: A checked custom exception must be declared or handled by the method that throws it.
15.explanation: A domain exception can name a business-rule failure more precisely than a generic exception. The method contract makes the checked failure explicit to callers.
